The foundational tension between σ-finiteness and measure uniqueness arises from the necessity of countable additivity in defining consistent extensions. Without σ-finiteness, the uniqueness of measure extensions fails, as demonstrated by counterexamples involving uncountable sets and their complements. This implies that in GSI, Bayesian posteriors must be constrained to σ-finite domains to ensure coherence. In GSE, state transitions must be defined within σ-finite subspaces to maintain deterministic evolution. The completion operator extends a measure to include negligible sets, ensuring completeness, but this process is only reliable under σ-finiteness. Inner measure duality provides a framework where inner and outer measures align under σ-finiteness, enabling precise characterization of measurable sets. When σ-finiteness is dropped, the duality breaks down, leading to pathological cases where every subset becomes measurable, undermining the theoretical foundation for both inference and reasoning.
